source.title: Robustifying Safety-Aligned Large Language Models through Clean Data Curation
source.authors: Xiao-Qun Liu; Jia-Cheng Liang; Mu-Chao Ye; Zhaohan Xi

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study runs harmful fine-tuning attacks and reports harmfulness and attack success rates, following the fine-tuning configuration in cited work [39], on additional models and with a data-curation condition.
record.gate_note: Only V1 is tested directly. The study does not measure response-position KL, compliant-prefix or suffix bypasses, localization in weights, or the cause of token-depth. Table 2 studies harmful data added during pre-training, not fine-tuning; a selection of its ASR results is recorded as findings outside the listed versions. Helpfulness results are not included because they do not measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: Attack II follows the configuration of [39]: 50 explicitly harmful (DEH) or 10 identity-shifting (DIS) examples. Table 3 reports AdvBench ASR and GPT-4 harmfulness after this harmful fine-tuning on four 6-8B models. The undefended column bears directly on V1. The paper is mainly a defence (C_TRL) evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that C_TRL (lowering perplexity of clean texts) strengthens safety alignment against harmful-data attacks in pre-training and in downstream fine-tuning. They add that gains are smaller for weaker models like ChatGLM-6B. Larger harmful fine-tuning sets overwhelm the defence. Efficacy depends on the available data, with safety samples helping further.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful fine-tuning datasets and reports attack success and harmfulness, following the cited configuration [39], but the paper focuses on testing C_TRL as a defence and adds curated-pretraining conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack dataset (DEH versus DIS), model, and whether pre-training used C_TRL-curated data change the reported attack success rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Injecting 5% harmful texts into simulated pre-training data raises AdvBench ASR to 74-98%. Adding C_TRL-curated clean texts lowers it to 14-38%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful data mixed into (continued) pre-training compromises safety, and low-perplexity curated data mitigates this.

fits_no_version.finding: C_TRL-curated pre-training lowers ASR after 50-DEH or 10-DIS fine-tuning, but harmful compliance stays at 33-84%. Gains are smallest on ChatGLM-6B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-training data curation only partly hardens models against few-shot harmful fine-tuning.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed results. The main fine-tuning comparisons measure a defence condition against no C_TRL rather than providing an un-fine-tuned safety baseline in Table 3.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2: omitted other Attack I ASR conditions (Vicuna-7B and ChatGLM-6B, and D10k conditions) because they are harmful-text injection during pre-training, outside the tested V1 fine-tuning version. Also omitted the paper's helpfulness-score results, which do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Only 10 or 50 examples are tested; the few-hundred range is shown only in Figure 7, whose values cannot be read. Models are 6-8B open models only. There is no pre-fine-tuning harmfulness baseline in Table 3.
Benign fine-tuning is not tested. Benign data breaking safety is only cited ([24, 39]).
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
C_TRL is a perplexity-based data defence, not token-depth deepening. It is not evaluated as spreading safety beyond early tokens.

missing.what: ASR as a function of harmful fine-tuning data volume on curated-pretrained models. Authors state larger harmful sets dominate regardless of C_TRL. Values are not readable in the text.
Safety baseline (ASR or Sharm) of each model before any harmful fine-tuning in the Attack II setting

record.verdict_notes: This is a defence paper. Its V1-relevant evidence is only the undefended Attack II column of Table 3, which replicates [39]'s setup on new models. The undefended models were first trained by the authors on D2k, and no pre-attack baseline is given. Vicuna-7B and ChatGLM-6B have weak safety training, so 'removes safety' is less informative for them. Table 4's Attack I w/o-C_TRL ASR (20.9% for Llama-3) is inconsistent in setup with Table 2 (81.5%), because Table 4 adds safety samples. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fine-tuning with 50 DEH examples or 10 DIS examples, not the full range up to a few hundred; results are limited to the reported datasets, models, and training conditions.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction data fine-tuned on a safety-trained model.
Does not measure per-token KL divergence or compare response positions.
Does not test compliant response prefixes, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Does not localize safety behaviour to weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuning with 50 DEH or 10 DIS examples, no C_TRL defence, on Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7B, Vicuna-7B and ChatGLM-6B
relationships.reason: ASR is 78.3-100% and Sharm 3.77-4.93 (R01, R02, R05, R06, R09, R10, R13, R14, R17, R18, R21, R22, R25, R26, R29, R30). There is no pre-fine-tune baseline in this table.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success was 78.3–100% and harmfulness scores 3.77–4.93 across the four models. This comparison reports no pre-fine-tuning baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuning without C_TRL pre-training curation, across the four models and both attack datasets
reader_labels.reason: The reported attack success rates are 78.3% to 100% after fine-tuning on 10 DIS or 50 DEH examples; harmfulness scores are also high (R01-R02, R05-R06, R09-R10, R13-R14, R17-R18, R21-R22, R25-R26, R29-R30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: C_TRL lowers attack success rates substantially, though harmful compliance remains; the effect therefore depends on the preceding data-curation condition (R03-R04, R07-R08, R11-R12, R15-R16, R19-R20, R23-R24, R27-R28, R31-R32).
